items.title: Xaluritamig Plus Abiraterone Phase 3 Trial for Metastatic CRPC
items.summary: This phase 3 trial is recruiting patients with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer who have not yet received chemotherapy. It compares xaluritamig (a new drug) combined with abiraterone against standard treatments including docetaxel, cabazitaxel, or abiraterone alone. The primary goal is to determine if the combination extends overall survival.

items.title: 177Lu-TLX591 Radioligand Therapy Phase 3 Trial for mCRPC
items.summary: This phase 3 trial is recruiting patients with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer who have progressed after androgen receptor pathway inhibitor treatment. It evaluates whether adding 177Lu-TLX591 (a radioligand therapy) to standard care improves outcomes compared to standard care alone. This is similar to existing PSMA-targeted radioligand therapies.

items.title: Apalutamide Plus Radiation Phase 3 Trial for Recurrent Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This phase 3 trial is recruiting patients whose prostate cancer has returned after surgery (biochemical recurrence). It tests whether adding apalutamide and abiraterone to standard radiation and hormone therapy improves outcomes. For patients with limited spread detected on PET scans, it also tests adding targeted radiation to those areas.

items.title: ZEN-3694 Plus Testosterone or Enzalutamide Trial for mCRPC
items.summary: This phase 2 trial is recruiting patients with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer resistant to multiple therapies. It tests a novel sequence: first combining testosterone with ZEN-3694 (targeting MYC protein), then switching to enzalutamide plus ZEN-3694. The approach aims to make tumors more sensitive to treatment by first using testosterone.

items.title: GSK5471713 First-in-Human Study for Metastatic CRPC
items.summary: This phase 1/2 trial is recruiting patients with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer to test GSK5471713, a completely new drug. The study will determine safe doses and evaluate early evidence of effectiveness. As a first-in-human trial, this represents an early-stage investigation of a novel mechanism.

items.title: GSK5458514 Study for Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This phase 1/2 trial is recruiting patients with prostate cancer to test GSK5458514 alone or combined with other treatments. The study will determine safe doses and evaluate effectiveness. This is an early-stage investigation of a new drug with an undisclosed mechanism.

items.title: Olaparib Plus Abiraterone Phase 3 Trial China Cohort
items.summary: This phase 3 trial in China has finished enrolling patients with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer who have not received chemotherapy or newer hormone agents at the mCRPC stage. It compares olaparib (a PARP inhibitor) plus abiraterone against abiraterone alone to evaluate effectiveness and side effects.

items.title: Cabazitaxel Plus Abiraterone Trial After Docetaxel for mCRPC
items.summary: This phase 2 trial has finished enrolling patients with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer previously treated with docetaxel. It compares abiraterone and antiandrogen therapy with or without adding cabazitaxel chemotherapy and prednisone to determine which approach is more effective.

items.title: REINFORCE Trial: Docetaxel for Non-Responders to Apalutamide
items.summary: This phase 3 trial is recruiting patients with metastatic hormone-sensitive prostate cancer who started apalutamide plus ADT but did not achieve deep PSA response. It tests whether adding docetaxel chemotherapy to their treatment improves outcomes. This represents a response-adapted treatment strategy.

items.title: Abemaciclib With or Without Atezolizumab Completed Trial for mCRPC
items.summary: This completed phase 2 trial tested abemaciclib (a targeted chemotherapy drug) alone or combined with atezolizumab (an immunotherapy) in patients with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer. The study evaluated whether these drugs could shrink tumors or prevent cancer growth and assessed safety of the combination.

items.title: ABBV-969 Phase 1 Study for Metastatic CRPC
items.summary: This phase 1 trial has finished enrolling patients with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer to test ABBV-969, an investigational drug given by IV infusion. The study is evaluating different doses to determine safety, how the drug moves through the body, and early signs of effectiveness.

items.title: SPARKLE Trial: PSMA Radioligand Therapy for Low-Volume Metastatic Disease
items.summary: This phase 2 trial will test 177Lu-PSMA-617 (a radioligand therapy) combined with hormone therapy in patients with hormone-sensitive prostate cancer that has spread to a limited number of sites or has returned after treatment. It compares different treatment combinations to standard hormone therapy alone.

items.title: Tarlatamab Trial for DLL3-Positive Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This phase 2 trial is recruiting patients with metastatic prostate cancer positive for Delta-like Protein 3 (DLL3) that has relapsed or not responded to treatment. The study tests tarlatamab, a drug that targets the DLL3 protein, to determine if it can effectively treat this specific subset of prostate cancer.

items.title: Low Dose Naltrexone Trial for Fatigue on Hormone Therapy
items.summary: This phase 2 trial will test whether low dose naltrexone (3 mg daily pill) can reduce fatigue in men with prostate cancer receiving androgen deprivation therapy. Patients may also be taking newer hormone medicines like apalutamide, enzalutamide, or abiraterone. This addresses a common quality of life issue during treatment.

items.title: Cediranib Plus Olaparib Trial for Metastatic CRPC
items.summary: This phase 2 trial has finished enrolling patients with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer to compare olaparib (a PARP inhibitor) alone versus combined with cediranib (an enzyme blocker). The combination approach targets DNA repair and blood vessel growth to potentially improve treatment effectiveness.

items.title: Ifinatamab Deruxtecan Study for Metastatic CRPC
items.summary: This phase 1/2 trial is recruiting patients with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer to test ifinatamab deruxtecan (I-DXd), an antibody-drug conjugate. The study evaluates I-DXd alone or combined with other treatments, assessing safety, determining optimal doses, and monitoring PSA levels as a measure of effectiveness.

items.title: Neo-DAB Completed Trial: Darolutamide Plus Abemaciclib
items.summary: This completed phase 1 trial tested the combination of darolutamide and abemaciclib with androgen deprivation therapy in patients with metastatic, non-metastatic, and advanced prostate cancer. The study established a recommended dose for the combination and evaluated its safety and effectiveness over a 6-month treatment period.

items.title: Mevrometostat Study for Castration-Resistant Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This phase 1 trial is recruiting men with castration-resistant prostate cancer who have progressed after previous CRPC treatment. The study tests mevrometostat alone or combined with enzalutamide. Mevrometostat targets cancer-promoting proteins and represents a novel treatment approach for resistant disease.

items.title: RECIPROCAL Trial: Adaptive Dosing for Lutetium-177 PSMA Therapy
items.summary: This phase 3 trial is recruiting patients with advanced hormone-resistant prostate cancer to test different dosing schedules for lutetium-177 Lu PSMA RLT. It compares standard every-6-week dosing versus personalized, extended intervals based on patient response, evaluating whether adaptive scheduling improves quality of life while maintaining effectiveness.

items.title: Ifinatamab Deruxtecan Phase 3 Trial for Metastatic Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This phase 3 trial is recruiting patients with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer to compare ifinatamab deruxtecan (I-DXd) against standard chemotherapy. The study will determine if patients receiving I-DXd live longer overall and live longer without cancer progression compared to those receiving chemotherapy.

items.title: Inflammation Pathways Drive Castration-Resistant Prostate Cancer Development
items.summary: This research review explains how chronic inflammation, particularly through NFκB and IL6/JAK/STAT3 signaling pathways, reshapes the genetic landscape of advanced prostate cancer. These inflammatory signals work with androgen receptor pathways to promote tumor survival, spread, and treatment resistance. Understanding these mechanisms may reveal new therapeutic targets for castration-resistant disease.

items.title: PSMA DNA Vaccine Enhances Immunotherapy Response in Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This preclinical study developed a nanoplasmid DNA vaccine targeting PSMA (a protein highly expressed in aggressive prostate cancer). The vaccine stimulated immune responses, prevented tumor growth and lung metastasis in models, and enhanced the effectiveness of PD-1 checkpoint blockade immunotherapy. This represents a potential new immunotherapy approach.

items.title: Dual BRD4/AKT Inhibitor Overcomes Treatment Resistance in mCRPC
items.summary: This research identified a new compound that blocks both BRD4 and AKT proteins simultaneously to overcome c-MYC-driven resistance in metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer. The dual inhibitor approach addresses a key resistance mechanism where AKT inhibitors alone often fail due to elevated c-MYC expression.

items.title: Meta-Analysis of Immunotherapy Effectiveness in Metastatic CRPC
items.summary: This comprehensive analysis of 21 clinical trials including 1,580 patients evaluated immune checkpoint inhibitors for metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer. Results showed 63% one-year survival and 41% six-month progression-free survival. Combinations of immunotherapy with other agents showed better outcomes than immunotherapy alone, though results remain preliminary for unselected mCRPC patients.

items.title: Zoledronic Acid Prevents Bone Loss in mHSPC Patients on Enzalutamide
items.summary: This phase 2 trial showed that metastatic hormone-sensitive prostate cancer patients receiving androgen deprivation therapy plus enzalutamide experienced significant bone mineral density loss after 18 months. Adding zoledronic acid (a bone-strengthening medication) prevented this bone loss at both the femoral neck and lumbar spine, supporting its use for skeletal health protection.
